_source: Plain-language summaries of SREGym's reference answers (experiments/frozen30-reference-answers.json) for hand labelling. Written from the reference text only; where a summary and the reference seem to differ, the reference wins.

revoke_auth_mongodb-1.name: Database access revoked
revoke_auth_mongodb-1.what: The geo service's database, `mongodb-geo`, had the service's access revoked. The service still starts, but every operation that reads or writes the database fails with authorization errors from MongoDB.
revoke_auth_mongodb-1.like: Your key card still opens the building, but your access to the records room was removed.
revoke_auth_mongodb-1.place: The `mongodb-geo` database (the access granted to the geo service).
revoke_auth_mongodb-1.cause: Database access was explicitly revoked, so database-backed operations fail with MongoDB authorization errors.
revoke_auth_mongodb-1.notblame: A crash at startup: the service starts normally.

search_rate_retry_collapse_hotel_reserva.name: Retry storm keeps the rate service overloaded
search_rate_retry_collapse_hotel_reserva.what: The `search` service calls the `rate` service with up to three attempts and a short deadline per attempt. A short burst of traffic filled `rate`'s bounded queue; calls then exceed their deadline but still use `rate`'s capacity, and `search` retries them. Internal load stays above capacity even after outside traffic is back to normal.
search_rate_retry_collapse_hotel_reserva.like: A busy call centre where every caller who waits ten seconds hangs up and calls back three times: the queue never clears, even after the rush.
search_rate_retry_collapse_hotel_reserva.place: The search-to-rate call path: search's retry and timeout policy together with rate's bounded queue.
search_rate_retry_collapse_hotel_reserva.cause: A timeout/retry/queue feedback loop keeps the overload going after the burst has ended.
search_rate_retry_collapse_hotel_reserva.notblame: Only "the rate limit is too low" (normal traffic is below it), or only the burst (it has ended). The reference counts this as incomplete.

service_dns_resolution_failure_social_ne.name: DNS refuses one service name
service_dns_resolution_failure_social_ne.what: The cluster's DNS server, CoreDNS, has a rule in its ConfigMap that answers "no such name" (NXDOMAIN) for `user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local`. Other services cannot find `user-service` by name, even though its pods are healthy and listening.
service_dns_resolution_failure_social_ne.like: The office directory lists a colleague as "no such person" while they sit at their desk.
service_dns_resolution_failure_social_ne.cause: An NXDOMAIN template for user-service's name makes in-cluster lookups of it fail.
service_dns_resolution_failure_social_ne.notblame: The `user-service` pods: they are healthy and listening.

configmap_drift_hotel_reservation.name: ConfigMap lost required keys
configmap_drift_hotel_reservation.what: The `geo` service's ConfigMap `geo-config` has drifted and is missing required keys, for example `GeoMongoAddress`. The `geo` deployment starts with incomplete settings, so it fails to connect to its dependencies and to handle requests that need those settings.
configmap_drift_hotel_reservation.like: A courier handed instructions with the delivery-address page torn out.
configmap_drift_hotel_reservation.cause: Required keys such as `GeoMongoAddress` are missing, so geo starts with incomplete configuration.
configmap_drift_hotel_reservation.notblame: Describing only the errors in geo without the missing keys.

duplicate_pvc_mounts_hotel_reservation.name: Replicas share a one-machine volume
duplicate_pvc_mounts_hotel_reservation.what: The `frontend` deployment was scaled to several replicas that all use one ReadWriteOnce volume claim, while a required anti-affinity rule forces the replicas onto different machines. The volume can be used on one machine only, so one replica runs and another stays Pending.
duplicate_pvc_mounts_hotel_reservation.like: Two people told to sit in different rooms while sharing one pair of headphones on a short cord.
duplicate_pvc_mounts_hotel_reservation.place: The `frontend` deployment (its replicas, the shared ReadWriteOnce claim and the hostname anti-affinity).
duplicate_pvc_mounts_hotel_reservation.cause: Several replicas reference one ReadWriteOnce, topology-bound claim while anti-affinity separates them, so only one can use it and the others stay Pending.
duplicate_pvc_mounts_hotel_reservation.notblame: A plain lack of nodes or resources: the conflict is between the shared volume and the anti-affinity.

node_conntrack_exhaustion_hotel_reservat.name: One machine's connection table is full
node_conntrack_exhaustion_hotel_reservat.what: A deployment, `edge-traffic-client`, is pinned to one worker machine and holds many TCP connections open to `rpc-gateway`. They fill that machine's Linux connection-tracking table (`nf_conntrack`), so new connections from that machine time out, even though Deployments, Pods, Services and Endpoints all look healthy.
node_conntrack_exhaustion_hotel_reservat.like: One guest keeps every outside line of a hotel switchboard busy: the phones work, but nobody else can place a call.
node_conntrack_exhaustion_hotel_reservat.place: The victim node's `nf_conntrack` table, filled by `edge-traffic-client`'s connections to `rpc-gateway`.
node_conntrack_exhaustion_hotel_reservat.cause: Held connections saturate the node's conntrack table, so new connections from that node time out.
node_conntrack_exhaustion_hotel_reservat.notblame: The Kubernetes objects (pods, services, endpoints): they look healthy.

network_policy_block.name: Network policy isolates a service
network_policy_block.what: A NetworkPolicy named `deny-all-recommendation` blocks all incoming and outgoing traffic for the `recommendation` pods. The pods keep running, but nothing can reach them and they reach nothing, so requests that need `recommendation` fail.
network_policy_block.like: A room locked from both sides: the person inside is fine, but nobody gets in or out.
network_policy_block.cause: The policy denies all ingress and egress for recommendation, isolating it.
network_policy_block.notblame: The recommendation pods themselves: they remain Running.

namespace_memory_limit.name: Namespace quota rejects new pods
namespace_memory_limit.what: A ResourceQuota, `memory-limit-quota`, on the `hotel-reservation` namespace requires every pod to declare memory, but the existing workloads do not. When the `search` deployment is recreated, its replacement pod is rejected with `must specify memory`. Pods that were already running keep running.
namespace_memory_limit.like: A new rule at the door: no entry without a declared weight limit. People inside stay; anyone who steps out cannot come back in.
namespace_memory_limit.place: ResourceQuota `memory-limit-quota` in `hotel-reservation` (`search` is the affected deployment).
namespace_memory_limit.cause: The quota enforces memory declarations the workloads lack, so admission rejects search's replacement pod.
namespace_memory_limit.notblame: A shortage of node memory: this is a policy rejection at admission.

service_wrong_pod_selection_hotel_reserv.name: Service also selects the wrong pods
service_wrong_pod_selection_hotel_reserv.what: The `frontend` Service's selector was broadened to `service-route=frontend`, a label that both the frontend pods and the `search` pods carry. Its endpoint list now includes a search pod, which listens on port 8082 instead of frontend's 5000, so some requests through the frontend Service land on a pod that cannot serve them.
service_wrong_pod_selection_hotel_reserv.like: A mail sorter that sends some of the shop's letters to the warehouse next door.
service_wrong_pod_selection_hotel_reserv.cause: The broadened selector adds a search pod to frontend's endpoints, so traffic intermittently reaches a pod that cannot serve it.
service_wrong_pod_selection_hotel_reserv.notblame: The frontend or search pods themselves.

mutating_webhook_resource_limits_social_.name: A webhook shrinks pod memory
mutating_webhook_resource_limits_social_.what: A cluster-wide MutatingWebhookConfiguration, `gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration`, intercepts every pod creation in `social-network` and rewrites the first container's memory request and limit to 16Mi. The Deployment still says 128Mi / 256Mi, but the running pods get 16Mi and are OOMKilled on start.
mutating_webhook_resource_limits_social_.like: A clerk who quietly rewrites every order form to the smallest size before it reaches the warehouse.
mutating_webhook_resource_limits_social_.cause: It patches the pods' memory to 16Mi at creation, so they are OOMKilled.
mutating_webhook_resource_limits_social_.notblame: The webhook backend server (it works as configured), the Deployment spec (its values are right), or the four inert companion webhooks.

finalizer_deadlock_controller_hotel_rese.name: Controller lost the right to finish a delete
finalizer_deadlock_controller_hotel_rese.what: ConfigMap `reservation-cleanup-token` is stuck in Terminating because of a finalizer owned by the `cleanup-controller` deployment. The ClusterRole `configmap-cleanup-controller` was made read-only, so the controller cannot patch ConfigMaps to remove the finalizer; its logs show HTTP 403 Forbidden.
finalizer_deadlock_controller_hotel_rese.like: A clerk must stamp a form before it can be shredded, but the stamp was taken away.
finalizer_deadlock_controller_hotel_rese.cause: The role lost permission to patch ConfigMaps, so the controller cannot remove the finalizer (403).
finalizer_deadlock_controller_hotel_rese.notblame: The controller's code: its normal loop works once its permissions are back.

cronjob_sidecar_blocks_completion_hotel_.name: A sidecar keeps every job running
cronjob_sidecar_blocks_completion_hotel_.what: The CronJob `audit-log-archiver` starts a pod every minute with two regular containers: `archiver`, which finishes quickly, and `fluent-bit-sidecar`, a log shipper that never exits. A Job completes only when every container ends, so each Job stays active forever and they pile up.
cronjob_sidecar_blocks_completion_hotel_.like: A meeting that cannot end because the note-taker never leaves the room.
cronjob_sidecar_blocks_completion_hotel_.cause: The sidecar is a regular container that never terminates, so the pods stay Running and the Jobs never complete and accumulate.

duplicate_pvc_mounts_social_network.name: Replicas share a one-machine volume (jaeger)
duplicate_pvc_mounts_social_network.what: The `jaeger` deployment was scaled to several replicas that all use one ReadWriteOnce volume claim, while a required anti-affinity rule forces the replicas onto different machines. The volume can be used on one machine only, so one replica runs and another stays Pending.
duplicate_pvc_mounts_social_network.like: Two people told to sit in different rooms while sharing one pair of headphones on a short cord.
duplicate_pvc_mounts_social_network.place: The `jaeger` deployment (its replicas, the shared ReadWriteOnce claim and the hostname anti-affinity).
duplicate_pvc_mounts_social_network.cause: Several replicas reference one ReadWriteOnce, topology-bound claim while anti-affinity separates them, so only one can use it and the others stay Pending.
duplicate_pvc_mounts_social_network.notblame: A plain lack of nodes or resources: the conflict is between the shared volume and the anti-affinity.

rolling_update_misconfigured_social_netw.name: A rollout removes all old pods first
rolling_update_misconfigured_social_netw.what: `custom-service`'s rollout strategy is `maxUnavailable=100%` with `maxSurge=0`, and the new pods' init container hangs. An update removes all old replicas before any new one is Ready, so the service stays unavailable.
rolling_update_misconfigured_social_netw.like: Closing every checkout lane to retrain the cashiers, while the trainees are stuck at the door.
rolling_update_misconfigured_social_netw.place: Deployment `custom-service` (its rollout strategy, together with the hanging init container).
rolling_update_misconfigured_social_netw.cause: maxUnavailable=100% and maxSurge=0 drain every old pod while the new pods' init container hangs, so nothing is Ready.
rolling_update_misconfigured_social_netw.notblame: Naming only one of the two parts: the reference names both the rollout settings and the hanging init container.

storage_user_unregistered-1.name: The database lost its user
storage_user_unregistered-1.what: The service logs in to `mongodb-geo` with the credentials it always used, but the expected database user is missing inside MongoDB, so it cannot authenticate and every storage operation fails.
storage_user_unregistered-1.like: Your gym card is fine, but the gym deleted your membership from its system.
storage_user_unregistered-1.place: The `mongodb-geo` database (the reference names the database, not the client service).
storage_user_unregistered-1.cause: The expected database user credentials are missing from MongoDB, so the dependent service cannot authenticate.
storage_user_unregistered-1.notblame: The client service's settings: the change is inside the database.

auth_miss_mongodb.name: Database TLS setup is broken
auth_miss_mongodb.what: `url-shorten-mongodb` requires TLS authentication, but its certificate setup is invalid, so clients cannot complete the TLS handshake and requests that need the database fail.
auth_miss_mongodb.like: A door that opens only with a badge, while the badge printer produces unreadable badges.
auth_miss_mongodb.cause: The certificate setup of a TLS-required MongoDB is invalid, so clients' TLS handshakes fail.
auth_miss_mongodb.notblame: The calling services: they fail because of the database's certificates.

missing_service_hotel_reservation.name: A database's Service was deleted
missing_service_hotel_reservation.what: The Kubernetes Service `mongodb-rate` was deleted, so other workloads cannot find or reach that database by name, even if its pods still exist.
missing_service_hotel_reservation.like: A shop that is still open, but its listing was removed from the map.
missing_service_hotel_reservation.cause: The Service is gone, so service discovery and routing to mongodb-rate fail.
missing_service_hotel_reservation.notblame: The mongodb-rate pods: they may still be running.

scale_pod_zero_social_net.name: A service scaled to zero
scale_pod_zero_social_net.what: Deployment `user-service` in `social-network` was scaled to zero replicas, so no pod serves it and every request that needs it fails at once.
scale_pod_zero_social_net.like: A shop with the lights on and the sign up, but no staff.
scale_pod_zero_social_net.cause: Replicas set to 0: there are no serving pods.
scale_pod_zero_social_net.notblame: Crashes or scheduling problems: there are simply no pods.

wrong_service_selector_hotel_reservation.name: Service selector matches no pods
wrong_service_selector_hotel_reservation.what: The `frontend` Service's selector has an extra, wrong label, so it no longer matches the frontend pods. The Service has no or too few endpoints, although the deployments look healthy.
wrong_service_selector_hotel_reservation.like: A receptionist told to send visitors to a desk number that does not exist.
wrong_service_selector_hotel_reservation.cause: A wrong label in the selector leaves the Service without matching endpoints.
wrong_service_selector_hotel_reservation.notblame: The frontend pods or deployment: they look healthy.

readiness_probe_misconfiguration_hotel_r.name: Readiness check points at a missing page
readiness_probe_misconfiguration_hotel_r.what: The `frontend` deployment's readiness probe checks `/healthz` on port `8080`, which does not exist. The pods never pass readiness, so Kubernetes keeps them out of the Service's endpoints even though the containers run.
readiness_probe_misconfiguration_hotel_r.like: An inspector who checks for a certificate on a wall that does not exist, so the shop is never cleared to open.
readiness_probe_misconfiguration_hotel_r.cause: The probe targets a non-existent endpoint (`/healthz` on 8080), so pods stay NotReady and get no traffic.
readiness_probe_misconfiguration_hotel_r.notblame: The frontend program itself: the containers may be running fine.

missing_configmap_hotel_reservation.name: A required ConfigMap was deleted
missing_configmap_hotel_reservation.what: A ConfigMap that the `mongodb-geo` deployment needs was deleted, so its pods start without required settings and fail to initialize or run with invalid defaults.
missing_configmap_hotel_reservation.like: Starting a machine after someone removed its settings card.
missing_configmap_hotel_reservation.cause: The ConfigMap is missing, so the pods lose required runtime configuration.

taint_no_toleration_social_network.name: The machines refuse the pods
taint_no_toleration_social_network.what: The cluster's machines carry the taint `sre-fault=blocked:NoSchedule`, but `user-service` only tolerates a different key (`dummy-key`), so its new pods cannot be placed anywhere and stay Pending.
taint_no_toleration_social_network.like: Every building has a "members only" sign, and the visitor's pass is for a different club.
taint_no_toleration_social_network.place: Deployment `user-service` (its tolerations) against the node taint.
taint_no_toleration_social_network.cause: Taint/toleration mismatch: the pods have no toleration for `sre-fault=blocked:NoSchedule`.
taint_no_toleration_social_network.notblame: A lack of capacity on the machines.

sidecar_port_conflict_hotel_reservation.name: A sidecar takes the app's port
sidecar_port_conflict_hotel_reservation.what: A sidecar container in the `frontend` pods listens on the same port as the main application, so the ports collide at startup and the pods do not become Ready.
sidecar_port_conflict_hotel_reservation.like: Two shops given the same street address.
sidecar_port_conflict_hotel_reservation.cause: The sidecar binds the same listening port as the primary container, causing a port conflict at startup.

init_container_dependency_hang_social_ne.name: An init container waits forever
init_container_dependency_hang_social_ne.what: `user-service` has an init container, `wait-for-legacy-config`, that loops on `nslookup legacy-config-service...` until it resolves. That Service no longer exists, so the loop never ends: new pods stay in `Init:0/1` and the rollout stalls, while the old pods keep serving.
init_container_dependency_hang_social_ne.like: Waiting at the door for a colleague who left the company months ago.
init_container_dependency_hang_social_ne.cause: The init container waits for `legacy-config-service`, which does not exist, so new pods never start.
init_container_dependency_hang_social_ne.notblame: The old pods: they still serve traffic.

misconfig_app_hotel_res.name: App configured with the wrong database port
misconfig_app_hotel_res.what: The `geo` deployment runs an image whose configuration connects to `mongodb-geo` on port 27777 instead of 27017. Geo panics when the connection fails and restarts again and again.
misconfig_app_hotel_res.like: Dialling the right person with the wrong extension.
misconfig_app_hotel_res.cause: Geo connects to mongodb-geo:27777 instead of 27017, so the database connection fails and geo panics.

wrong_bin_usage.name: The container starts the wrong program
wrong_bin_usage.what: The `profile` deployment's container entrypoint points to the wrong service binary, so an unintended program runs and profile's APIs misbehave or fail.
wrong_bin_usage.like: A vending machine wired so the coffee button dispenses soup.
wrong_bin_usage.cause: The entrypoint starts the wrong service binary.

update_incompatible_correlated.name: All databases upgraded to a bad version
update_incompatible_correlated.what: Six MongoDB deployments (`mongodb-geo`, `-profile`, `-rate`, `-recommendation`, `-reservation`, `-user`) were upgraded to an incompatible image, `mongo:8.0.14-rc0`, causing database failures across services.
update_incompatible_correlated.like: Every office replaced its filing cabinets with a model the clerks' keys do not fit.
update_incompatible_correlated.cause: An upgrade to an incompatible image version (`mongo:8.0.14-rc0`).
update_incompatible_correlated.notblame: A problem in one database only: the change hit all of them together.

ephemeral_port_range_hotel_reservation.name: Pods have only four outgoing ports
ephemeral_port_range_hotel_reservation.what: Every hotel-reservation pod sets `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to `32000 32003`, which leaves four ports for outgoing connections. The frontend cannot open connections to all its gRPC backends; at least one is always unreachable (`EADDRNOTAVAIL`), while pods keep running.
ephemeral_port_range_hotel_reservation.like: A switchboard with only four outside lines for a whole office.
ephemeral_port_range_hotel_reservation.cause: The ephemeral port range is narrowed to 4 ports, so outbound connections fail with EADDRNOTAVAIL.

file_descriptor_exhaustion.name: Too many connections for the open-file limit
file_descriptor_exhaustion.what: An outside load generator opens about 1,100 simultaneous TCP connections to `frontend`, whose container allows only 1,024 open files (`ulimit -n`). The frontend drops connections and logs "too many open files".
file_descriptor_exhaustion.like: A restaurant with 1,024 seats and 1,100 guests at the door.
file_descriptor_exhaustion.cause: A `ulimit -n` of 1024 is too low for the ~1,100 connections. The reference names the limit as the root cause.

latent_sector_error.name: Unreadable sectors under the database
latent_sector_error.what: The storage under `mongodb-geo` developed unreadable regions in its data files. WiredTiger's reads of those blocks fail, and `mongod` aborts on every start, so the database stays in CrashLoopBackOff until its data is restored.
latent_sector_error.like: A book with some pages glued shut: the reader stops at the first one it cannot open.
latent_sector_error.cause: Latent sector errors: data blocks cannot be read, so mongod aborts at start.
